title: Word-boundary matching for sentiment keywords
summary: score_sentiment() originally used substring counting (text.count("miss")), which matched "miss" inside unrelated words like "transmission" and "commission". Live Jackson Hole coverage tripped this exact bug. Replaced with \b-bounded regex matching across the whole lexicon.
impact: Eliminated false-positive sentiment hits that were inflating both score magnitude and confidence on noise, not signal.

title: Domain-specific sentiment lexicons (earnings vs. macro)
summary: The same word can carry opposite market meaning depending on context: "weak" earnings are bearish for a stock, but "weak" jobs/macro data is typically dovish (raises rate-cut odds) and so bullish for risk assets. Split into EARNINGS_LEXICON and MACRO_LEXICON, routed by event_type.
impact: Prevents a single shared keyword list from scoring macro commentary backwards.

title: Consensus-based confidence, not raw keyword-hit count
summary: Confidence originally scaled with total keyword hits, so one fact restated across several near-duplicate search snippets looked like multiple independent confirmations. Added snippet deduplication (difflib similarity ratio) before scoring, and confidence now reflects agreement across distinct, non-duplicate sources.
impact: A repeated single fact now yields meaningfully lower confidence than several genuinely distinct corroborating sources with the same total hit count.

title: Macro events need a real underlying to trade options on
summary: Macro events (Jackson Hole, FOMC, CPI) carry ticker=None in the Event schema by design -- they're not stock-specific. Feeding None straight into an Alpaca options/quote call crashed with a Pydantic validation error the first time it was exercised live. Added MACRO_PROXY_TICKER (SPY) as the resolved underlying whenever event.ticker is None.
impact: Caught via live verification before Aug 28, not in production. Jackson Hole (and any future macro event) now trades SPY options as the broad-market proxy.

title: Contract expiration filtering must happen server-side, not client-side
summary: select_contract() originally queried expiration_date_gte=today and filtered the target DTE window client-side after the fact. For names with dense near-term expirations (SPY lists near-daily expiries), a single contract page came back entirely near-zero-DTE strikes before ever reaching the target window -- select_contract returned None even though valid contracts existed. Fixed by setting expiration_date_gte directly in the API request instead of filtering after the fact.
impact: Found live against the real paper account testing the SPY macro-proxy path -- would have silently produced 'no contract found' for the flagship Jackson Hole trade.

title: Position size vs. real option premiums
summary: Live verification showed the original per-trade budget frequently couldn't afford a single ATM contract at real SPY/NVDA premiums, let alone both legs of a straddle -- trades were silently sized to qty=0 and skipped. Increased the per-trade equity allocation and added an explicit _check_min_trade_budget gate that logs a distinct "SKIPPED: ..." message (not folded into a generic no-trade log) whenever a signal clears every eligibility/confidence/sentiment gate but can't be sized.
impact: Prevents the failure mode of 'the system went quiet' being ambiguous between 'nothing qualified' and 'something qualified but couldn't be sized' -- critical for reading the system correctly live during a demo.

title: Exit logic is take-profit and max-hold only -- deliberately no stop-loss
summary: Before this, positions opened and simply sat until expiry with no automated exit at all. Added check_and_close_positions(), polled every cycle: closes a position once its unrealized gain reaches a configurable take-profit threshold, or once it's within a configurable number of days of expiring (to avoid pin risk/illiquidity right at expiration). Deliberately did NOT add a stop-loss or any loss-triggered exit. This is not an oversight: every position Daedalus opens is a bought (long) call, put, or straddle -- never written/sold -- so loss per trade is already bounded to the premium paid by construction. A stop-loss would realize that already-bounded loss early on paths that might otherwise recover, cutting into the exact convexity the premium bought.
impact: Positions no longer ride to expiry unmanaged on the upside or the max-hold/pin-risk side, without introducing a loss-triggered exit that would work against the defined-risk, long-only design the entry side already guarantees.
